summary_en: Comparables, ownership, transactions, rents, footfall and the datasets other products are built on.
summary_fr: Comparables, propriétaires, transactions, loyers, fréquentation et les jeux de données sur lesquels d'autres produits sont bâtis.

tools.name: ATTOM Data
tools.positioning: A national property data warehouse sold as bulk files and APIs — the plumbing under other people's products.
tools.description: ATTOM licenses standardised property data covering the large majority of the US population: tax assessor records, deeds and transfers, mortgages, foreclosures, AVM values, neighbourhood and hazard data. It sells to builders of products rather than to end users, through bulk delivery, cloud shares and APIs.
tools.real_estate_use: When a proptech product shows an owner's name, last sale price and estimated value on a property page, the data underneath is often licensed rather than collected. ATTOM is one of the standard suppliers for that layer, the alternative being to build a county-by-county pipeline yourself. Lenders and insurers use the same feeds for portfolio monitoring.
features: Tax assessor and recorder records at national coverage
Deed, mortgage, foreclosure and pre-foreclosure events
AVM property valuations and equity estimates
Neighbourhood, school and natural-hazard data
Delivery by API, bulk file and cloud data share
Property-level identifiers for record matching

use_cases.job: Screen a national portfolio for equity position and foreclosure risk
Power a product's property pages without building a county data pipeline

tools.name: Cherre
tools.positioning: Not another data source — the layer that reconciles the twenty you already pay for onto one property identity.
tools.description: Cherre is a real estate data management platform. It ingests a firm's internal systems and its licensed third-party feeds, resolves them to a common property and entity identity, and exposes the result to BI tools and models. The product is the resolution and the connectors, not the underlying data.
tools.real_estate_use: A large owner-operator typically has the rent roll in Yardi, valuations in ARGUS, market data from a vendor and a dozen spreadsheets — with no shared key between them. Cherre matches them to one property record so that portfolio reporting stops being a quarterly manual reconciliation, and so that a model can be trained on something coherent.
features: Entity and address resolution to a single property identity
Prebuilt connectors to major real estate systems and data vendors
Managed warehouse with governed access
Data quality monitoring and lineage
Delivery to BI tools, notebooks and applications
Marketplace of third-party datasets

use_cases.job: Consolidate portfolio reporting across accounting, valuation and market systems
Give analysts one governed dataset instead of eight incompatible exports

tools.name: Cityscan
tools.positioning: Everything around an address, scored — noise, pollution, transport, schools, risks, amenities — in one page.
tools.description: Cityscan aggregates public and private data about the environment of a French address — transport, education, amenities, noise, air quality, natural and technological risks, planning projects — into scores and reports embeddable into professional products.
tools.real_estate_use: Location quality is the argument every French listing makes and none evidences. Cityscan turns it into a scored report an agency can attach to a listing or a valuation, and that a developer or an investor can use to compare two sites. It also surfaces what a seller would rather not mention: a planned road, a flood risk, a nearby industrial site.
features: Environmental and amenity scoring per address
Transport, education and services accessibility analysis
Noise, air quality and pollution indicators
Natural and technological risk exposure
Planned urban projects near the address
Embeddable reports and widgets for professionals

use_cases.job: Evidence the quality of a location instead of asserting it in the listing text
Compare two candidate sites on environmental and risk criteria

tools.name: CLAMEUR
tools.positioning: French private-rental rent observatory built from signed leases collected at source, with a mapping application for members and free published trends.
tools.description: CLAMEUR is an association that produces an observatory of rents in the French private rental sector. It collects signed leases through partnerships with professional unions, federations, networks and managers rather than from advertisements, and states it holds more than a million references per year. Free national, regional, departmental and metropolitan trend pages publish rents excluding charges and their four-year evolution by property type. Members and contributors additionally get a web application with mapped navigation, indicators, charts, an advanced geolocated search and access to the underlying lease references down to municipality and IRIS zone level. Bespoke studies can be commissioned.
tools.real_estate_use: Rent evidence in France is scarce outside the regulated observatories, and portal asking prices are not the same thing as signed rents. CLAMEUR is the counter-evidence: it is built from executed leases handed over by managers, so a letting agent pricing a lot, a landlord arguing an indexation, or an investor testing a yield assumption can cite an actual market rent for the commune rather than an advertised one. The granularity down to IRIS zone is what makes it usable in cities where two neighbourhoods a kilometre apart do not rent alike. Local authorities and rent-control policy work use it for the same reason — it is one of the few sources covering medium-sized towns and rural areas.
features: Rent observatory built from signed leases collected through professional partners
Free national, regional, departmental and metropolitan trend pages with four-year evolution
Member web application with mapped navigation and charted indicators
Granularity down to municipality and IRIS zone
Advanced geolocated search over lease references
Commissioned bespoke studies

use_cases.job: Price a rental lot against signed rents in the same commune rather than against portal asking prices
Test a rental yield assumption on a medium-sized town that commercial datasets barely cover

tools.name: CoStar
tools.positioning: The commercial property database the industry underwrites against, built on a research organisation rather than on scraping.
tools.description: CoStar maintains a researched inventory of US commercial buildings — physical characteristics, ownership, tenancy, lease comparables, sale comparables, availabilities and submarket analytics — collected and verified by a large in-house research team and sold as a subscription with strict per-seat licensing.
tools.real_estate_use: It is the reference for the questions that precede a deal: what is the true rentable area, who owns the entity behind the LLC, what did the last three comparable leases sign at, what is the submarket vacancy trend. Brokers pull comparables for a pitch, investors size a market before underwriting, lenders sanity-check a borrower's rent roll.
features: Researched property records with ownership and tenancy detail
Lease and sale comparables with confirmed terms
Availability and vacancy tracking by submarket
Market analytics, forecasts and rent trends
Tenant tracking and expiring-lease intelligence
Directory of owners, brokers and tenants

use_cases.job: Size a submarket and pull comparable leases before underwriting an acquisition
Build a pitch on confirmed comparables rather than on asking rents

tools.name: Crexi
tools.positioning: A CRE marketplace that also runs the deal — listing, bidding, due diligence room and comps in one place.
tools.description: Crexi combines a commercial listing marketplace with transaction tooling: offer management, an auction platform, a virtual deal room, and Crexi Intelligence for sales comparables, ownership records and lease data. It positions itself as the challenger to the incumbent CoStar and LoopNet pairing.
tools.real_estate_use: A broker lists an asset, receives structured offers or runs a timed auction, and shares due-diligence documents through a permissioned data room instead of a shared drive link. Buyers use Crexi Intelligence to check what comparable assets traded for and who owns the building next door before committing to underwriting.
features: Commercial listing marketplace across asset classes
Structured offer submission and auction platform
Permissioned virtual due-diligence rooms
Crexi Intelligence comparables, ownership and lease data
Broker CRM and buyer activity analytics
Marketing tools including flyers and email campaigns

use_cases.job: Run a competitive bid process on an asset with a controlled document room
Check sale comparables and ownership before underwriting an acquisition

tools.name: DVF — Demandes de valeurs foncières
tools.positioning: Every French property transaction of the last five years, published as open data by the tax administration — free, and the base layer under most French valuation products.
tools.description: DVF publishes the property transactions registered by the French tax administration: address, date, price, surface, property type and land parcel, covering most of the country and updated twice a year. It is available as bulk open data, through a public API and through a free map application.
tools.real_estate_use: It is the closest thing France has to public sale comparables. An agent checks what the flat two floors down actually sold for, an investor tests a seller's price claim, an appraiser builds a comparables table with a verifiable public source. Its limits matter as much: Alsace-Moselle and Mayotte are excluded, sales are registered several months late, and the price is the recorded transfer price, not the negotiated market story behind it.
features: Registered transaction price, date, surface and property type
Coverage of most of France over a rolling five-year window
Free bulk open data download and public API
Free map application for address-level consultation
Land parcel references linking to cadastral data
Open licence permitting commercial reuse

use_cases.job: Check what comparable properties in the building actually sold for
Build a comparables table on a source the client can verify independently

tools.name: Fluximmo
tools.positioning: French property listings as an API — the raw feed behind pige tools and market products.
tools.description: Fluximmo collects real estate listings published across French portals and classified sites, deduplicates them, distinguishes private from professional sellers, and delivers the result as a structured API with history and change tracking.
tools.real_estate_use: It is infrastructure rather than an end-user product: a pige tool, a market study or an internal prospecting system uses the feed instead of scraping portals themselves. The deduplication and private-versus-professional classification are the hard parts, since the same property appears repeatedly under different descriptions and prices.
features: Aggregated listing feed across French portals and classified sites
Deduplication of the same property across sources
Private versus professional seller classification
Price change and listing lifecycle history
Geographic and criteria-based filtering
REST API delivery with historical access

use_cases.job: Build a prospecting or market product on a listing feed instead of scraping portals
Feed an internal canvassing system with deduplicated private-seller listings

tools.name: HouseCanary
tools.positioning: Valuation sold with its confidence interval, for people who have to act on the number.
tools.description: HouseCanary provides residential automated valuations, forecast values, rental estimates and condition-adjusted appraisals, delivered by API and through analyst-facing products. Its output is designed for institutional use — every value comes with an accuracy band.
tools.real_estate_use: An iBuyer or a single-family rental fund cannot send an appraiser to every candidate house. It prices thousands of addresses a week through an AVM, and the confidence interval decides which ones get a human inspection. Lenders use the same feeds for portfolio monitoring and collateral review between full appraisals.
features: Residential AVM with confidence scoring
Three-year value and rent forecasts by block and metro
Rental value estimation
Condition-adjusted valuation products
Market analytics down to block group
Delivery by API and bulk file

use_cases.job: Price thousands of candidate homes a week and flag the ones needing a human look
Monitor collateral value across a loan portfolio between full appraisals

tools.name: Kel Foncier
tools.positioning: Land prospecting for French developers — which parcels can be built on, how much, and who owns them.
tools.description: Kel Foncier combines cadastral parcels, local urban planning rules, building rights, ownership data, building permits and transactions into a mapping and search tool for property developers and land prospectors.
tools.real_estate_use: A French development starts with a question the PLU answers slowly: on this parcel, what height, what footprint, what constraints. Kel Foncier makes that searchable in reverse — find every parcel in a commune with unused building rights above a threshold, filter out the protected ones, and get the owner. It compresses weeks of town-hall work into a query.
features: Cadastral parcels with local planning rules applied
Residual building rights calculation per parcel
Ownership information and owner typology
Building permit history and pipeline
Transaction and land price references
Prospecting lists, alerts and export

use_cases.job: Find parcels with unused building rights in a target commune and identify the owners
Test the development potential of a site before making an offer

tools.name: ListHub
tools.positioning: Listing syndication and reporting for MLSs, brokers and agents, plus a normalized MLS data feed for the publishers that display those listings.
tools.description: ListHub is a syndication platform operated by Move, Inc. that takes listing data out of a multiple listing service and distributes it to a network of more than 170 real estate websites. It serves two sides of the same pipe: on one side MLSs, brokerages and agents who decide where their listings travel and who read back performance reports on each destination; on the other side publishers, who consume MLS content through a customizable API covering sources in all fifty states under a single contract, delivered in RESO-normalized form. A separate Global offering pushes listings to overseas audiences, and a Connector product synchronizes with Realogy's database.
tools.real_estate_use: A broker of record who has just signed a listing does not want to re-key it into every portal, and does not want it appearing on sites they never agreed to. They connect their MLS feed to ListHub once, then use the dashboard to opt each publisher in or out, and read the per-site reporting to see which destinations actually produced views and leads before renewing anything. On the other side of the same platform, a portal or a regional real estate magazine that needs live inventory subscribes to the publisher API rather than negotiating with hundreds of MLSs one by one.
features: Listing syndication to a network of over 170 real estate websites
Per-publisher opt-in and opt-out control for brokers
Listing performance reporting across destination sites
Publisher API delivering RESO-normalized MLS data from all 50 states
ListHub Global for international listing distribution
Connector synchronization with Realogy's database

use_cases.job: Decide site by site where the office's listings are syndicated, and withdraw from a publisher without touching the MLS entry
Check which destination websites generated views on a listing before renewing an advertising commitment
Source live, normalized MLS listing data through one API instead of contracting with each MLS separately

tools.name: MeilleursAgents
tools.positioning: The French price map the public consults — and the seller-lead engine agencies buy on the strength of it.
tools.description: MeilleursAgents publishes street-level price estimates across France from notarial and market data, offers owners a free online valuation, and sells agencies visibility and seller leads generated by those valuation requests, alongside agency comparison and review features.
tools.real_estate_use: It changed the French listing appointment. An owner arrives having already read a neighbourhood price per square metre, so the agent's pricing conversation starts from a public reference rather than from a blank page. On the professional side, an owner who requested a valuation is a seller lead with intent, which is what agencies actually pay for.
features: Street and neighbourhood level price indices
Free online valuation for owners
Seller lead generation and delivery to agencies
Agency visibility, profiles and reviews
Market trend indicators by city and district
Agency performance comparison for consumers

use_cases.job: Buy seller leads from owners who have just requested a valuation
Get a reference price for a property before meeting an agency

capabilities: Automated valuation from transaction and market data

tools.name: Placer.ai
tools.positioning: Foot traffic as a leasing argument — how many people actually walk into this centre, and where else do they go.
tools.description: Placer.ai turns anonymised mobile location data into visit metrics for physical venues: visit counts, dwell time, trade-area maps, visitor demographics and cross-shopping between brands. Coverage is strongest in the US, with an expanding international footprint.
tools.real_estate_use: In retail leasing it replaces the argument from intuition. A landlord shows a prospective tenant that the centre draws a measured number of visits from a trade area matching the brand's customer profile. Investors use the same data to underwrite retail assets and to spot decline before it appears in the rent roll.
features: Visit counts and trends per venue and per chain
Trade-area maps and visitor origin analysis
Visitor demographics and psychographic segments
Cross-visitation between brands and centres
Site selection scoring for new locations
Void analysis and competitive benchmarking

use_cases.job: Underwrite a retail asset on measured footfall rather than on reported sales
Prove trade-area quality to a retail tenant during lease negotiation

capabilities: Visit estimation models from mobile location panels

tools.name: Preventimmo
tools.positioning: Produit les documents réglementaires d'urbanisme et de risques attachés à une vente — ERP, ENSA, note d'urbanisme, droits de préemption — à partir d'une base tenue à jour.
tools.description: Preventimmo, part of the Septeo group, maintains a continuously updated database of French planning and environmental-risk data and turns it into the regulatory documents a property sale requires. Its catalogue covers the état des risques et pollutions, the état des nuisances sonores aériennes, the état des risques et pollutions des sols, a clay-shrinkage risk summary, notes de renseignements d'urbanisme, pre-emption rights, certificates and cadastral concordance. The same data is delivered three ways: the customer produces documents themselves online, delegates production to Preventimmo's own team, or connects directly to the underlying regulatory database for their own use. The vendor states sixteen years of activity, 106 staff and 5,000 active customers.
tools.real_estate_use: A notary preparing a deed, or an agent taking a mandate, has to attach an état des risques that is both current and defensible — and the underlying planning and risk data changes at the commune level without notice. Rather than querying prefecture and municipal sources by hand, they generate the ERP and the urban planning note from Preventimmo in a few clicks and attach them to the file. A diagnostics firm doing this at volume delegates the production entirely, or plugs its own software into the regulatory database so the documents appear inside the tool its technicians already use. When a sale is later contested on a disclosure point, the documents carry a traceable source and date.
features: État des risques et pollutions (ERP) généré en ligne
État des nuisances sonores aériennes (ENSA) et état des risques des sols (ERPS)
Notes de renseignements d'urbanisme et droits de préemption
Synthèse risques argiles et concordance cadastrale
Production déléguée des documents par les équipes de l'éditeur
Accès direct à la base réglementaire pour intégration dans un logiciel tiers

use_cases.job: Attacher à un acte des documents d'urbanisme et de risques conformes et datés, sans interroger chaque source publique
Produire l'ERP d'un bien au moment de la prise de mandat pour tenir l'obligation d'information de l'acquéreur
Alimenter son propre logiciel de diagnostic depuis la base réglementaire plutôt que de ressaisir les données

tools.name: PriceHubble
tools.positioning: Valuation and property analytics sold as an API and white-label modules, embedded in someone else's product.
tools.description: PriceHubble provides automated valuation, rental estimation, market analytics and property dashboards across several European countries, delivered as APIs and embeddable modules for banks, agencies, asset managers and proptech products rather than as a consumer site.
tools.real_estate_use: A French bank assessing collateral, an agency offering an instant valuation on its own site, or a portfolio holder revaluing quarterly all need the same computation without building it. PriceHubble sells that computation to be embedded, which is why it appears inside products whose users never see the brand.
features: Automated valuation for sale and rental values
Property dashboards and market analytics modules
White-label valuation widgets for websites
Portfolio revaluation and monitoring
Building and environment data enrichment
REST API delivery across European markets

use_cases.job: Value collateral and revalue a loan portfolio without building a model
Offer an instant valuation on the agency's own website to capture seller leads

tools.name: RealPage
tools.positioning: The broadest multifamily suite in the market — and the one whose revenue management product put algorithmic rent pricing under legal scrutiny.
tools.description: RealPage sells a wide portfolio for multifamily and single-family rental operators: property management systems (OneSite, Propertyware, Buildium), leasing and marketing, screening, utility management, asset optimisation and the AI Revenue Management products descended from YieldStar and LRO.
tools.real_estate_use: Large operators use it for the modules they cannot easily build: screening at scale, utility recovery, and above all revenue management — a model that recommends a rent for every unit every day based on market and portfolio signals. That last product is the subject of US antitrust litigation over algorithmic pricing, which is now part of any serious evaluation of it.
features: OneSite property management and accounting
AI Revenue Management rent pricing recommendations
Applicant screening and fraud detection
Utility billing and expense recovery
Leasing, marketing and contact centre services
Asset and portfolio performance analytics

use_cases.job: Price thousands of units daily against market and occupancy signals
Benchmark asset performance against a national multifamily dataset

tools.name: Reonomy
tools.positioning: Off-market prospecting — who owns this building, and how do I reach the human behind the LLC.
tools.description: Reonomy assembles public records, mortgage and lien filings, and contact data into a searchable database of US commercial properties, with a resolution layer that links a title-holding entity to the individuals actually behind it. Acquired by Altus Group.
tools.real_estate_use: Its use is prospecting rather than underwriting. A broker looking for listings filters a county for owners who have held an asset more than ten years with a maturing loan, then pulls a phone number for the principal — a list that would otherwise take weeks of county records work. Debt brokers run the same query against loan maturity dates.
features: Ownership resolution from LLC to individual principal
Contact records including phone and email for owners
Mortgage, lien and transaction history from public records
Portfolio view of everything an owner holds nationally
Saved searches with alerts on ownership or debt changes
Property-level physical and tax detail

use_cases.job: Build an off-market listing pipeline from long-held assets with maturing debt
Target owners whose loans mature in the next eighteen months

tools.name: Urbanease
tools.positioning: Land prospecting with the canvassing workflow attached — from the parcel to the owner letter.
tools.description: Urbanease provides French developers, land prospectors and local authorities with a mapping platform combining cadastre, urban planning documents, ownership data and constraints, together with prospecting workflow: parcel qualification, owner contact and canvassing follow-up.
tools.real_estate_use: Finding the parcel is half the job; the other half is a disciplined approach to an owner who was not thinking of selling. Urbanease keeps the qualification and the contact history on the parcel itself, so a prospector returning to a commune two years later knows who was already approached, by whom, and what they said.
features: Cadastral and urban planning mapping with constraints
Parcel qualification and development potential assessment
Owner identification and contact management
Canvassing history and follow-up per parcel
Territory and team assignment
Export and reporting for prospecting campaigns

use_cases.job: Run a disciplined land canvassing campaign with history kept on each parcel
Assess planning constraints and potential on a site before acquisition

tools.name: VTS
tools.positioning: The leasing pipeline for office landlords — every tour, proposal and lease in one view, plus a demand index nobody else has.
tools.description: VTS is a leasing and asset management platform for commercial landlords: deal pipeline, space availability, tenant and broker activity, portfolio reporting, and the VTS Market and Activate products covering marketing and tenant experience. Its VTS Office Demand Index derives leading indicators from platform activity.
tools.real_estate_use: Office leasing runs on a pipeline that traditionally lived in a leasing director's spreadsheet. VTS makes it institutional: every requirement, tour and proposal is tracked, so an asset manager can forecast occupancy and compare a proposed deal against portfolio standards. Because a large share of US office space transacts on the platform, aggregated tour activity becomes a market signal weeks ahead of signed-lease data.
features: Leasing deal pipeline with tours, proposals and approvals
Space availability and stacking plans
Portfolio occupancy and lease expiry reporting
VTS Market for online marketing of available space
VTS Activate tenant experience application
Office Demand Index from aggregated platform activity

use_cases.job: Forecast occupancy from a real leasing pipeline rather than from a spreadsheet
Track every requirement and proposal on a landlord's portfolio in one system

tools.name: Yanport
tools.positioning: The French listing and transaction database professionals use when the public price indices are not enough.
tools.description: Yanport collects and structures French property listings and transaction data over time — asking prices, price changes, time on market, withdrawal and sale outcomes — and delivers it through analysis tools and APIs to professionals and product builders.
tools.real_estate_use: France has no MLS, so the history of what was actually asked and what actually sold is fragmented across portals and public records. Yanport reconstructs it: an appraiser or a developer can see how long comparable properties took to sell and how far the asking price moved, which is the evidence a public price index cannot give.
features: Historic French listing database with price change tracking
Time on market and sale outcome analysis
Transaction data enrichment
Market analysis tools by sector and property type
API delivery for integration into products
Custom studies and portfolio analysis

use_cases.job: Show how far comparable asking prices moved before a sale actually closed
Assess absorption and pricing in a sector before committing to an operation
